Implement probes as exception-safe transactions: snapshot Python `random.getstate()`, NumPy `get_state()`, Torch CPU `get_rng_state()`, active CUDA `get_rng_state(device)`, and every explicit generator’s state; restore everything in `finally`. NumPy `Generator` instances require separate `bit_generator.state` snapshots. `torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[device_index])` handles Torch CPU/CUDA restoration, but excludes Python, NumPy and explicit generators. Use dedicated probe RNGs and cache fixed users, sequences, positives, negative samples and ordered candidate arrays for paired comparisons. These are implementation recommendations based on the documented [Torch RNG APIs](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/random.html), [Python state APIs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/random.html), and [NumPy generators](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/generator.html).

Save `(module, module.training)` for every module before calling `model.eval()`; evaluate under `torch.no_grad()` and restore each saved flag individually. Calling only `model.train(previous_root_flag)` destroys mixed child modes. Custom `train()` side effects and mutable forward caches need architecture-specific restoration; disabling gradients alone does not prevent state mutation. [PyTorch evaluation semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/autograd.html).

Avoid consuming the live training loader: use cached tensors or an independent diagnostic loader with its own generator, preferably `num_workers=0`. Restoring a loader generator cannot rewind sampler cursors, prefetched batches, worker RNGs, persistent dataset state or an active iterator; exact rollback needs explicit checkpoint support for these states. PyTorch documents [worker seeding, generator consumption and prefetching](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html). The host-specific contract must separately document `DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, returning metrics and metric definitions, with `view.model` as the actual trained module and loader batches `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` of shape B×L.
